algorithm_validation.expected_contextual_preferences: agents 0,1,2 are respectively optimal for one-hot contexts 0,1,2

hls_evaluation.scenario: HLS contextual agent selection; 3 tasks, 3 heterogeneous agents; fixed competencies
hls_evaluation.demand: existing C5 NonStationaryTaskDemand; three equal-length phases with distributions (0.70,0.20,0.10), (0.10,0.20,0.70), (0.20,0.70,0.10)
hls_evaluation.context_features: 3-dimensional one-hot task identity; same task context supplied for every agent to LinUCB
hls_evaluation.reward: Bernoulli task success in [0,1], sampled from fixed agent-task competence; per-agent-period potential outcomes pre-generated and shared across policies
hls_evaluation.learning_scope: LinUCB learns per-agent reward-model coefficients only; physical agent competencies remain fixed
hls_evaluation.linucb_variant: disjoint linear models, Li et al. (2010) §3.1, Algorithm 1; tie break is lowest agent index
hls_evaluation.exp3: existing unmodified EXP3 implementation; context-free by algorithm definition
hls_evaluation.uniform: uniform random agent selection, with independent policy RNG
hls_evaluation.best_fixed_mapping: best realized fixed task-to-agent map among all 27 mappings; retrospective evaluator-only reference
hls_evaluation.contextual_oracle: selects the agent with highest true expected reward for each observed task; evaluator-only model-knowledge reference, does not inspect realized potential outcome
hls_evaluation.information_boundary: LinUCB receives current task features and only selected reward; EXP3/uniform receive no context features; all receive only their selected reward as action feedback
